chunks: And as for what was narrated: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf from Sa'dan ibn Muslim from Ali al-Wasiti who said:

The young wife entered, and she was under the authority of Isa ibn Musa, upon the Imam (peace be upon him). She was virtuous. She said: 'I am perfuming myself for my husband, so I put wine in the comb with which I comb my hair, and I place it on my head.' He said: 'There is no harm in that.'
So it does not contradict the first report, because it is to be understood according to the meaning narrated in it.

key_terms.عِيسَى بْنُ مُوسَى: Isa ibn Musa, a companion of the Imams

ai.seo_question: Is wine considered impure if used for perfume on the body?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) validates the permissibility of using wine as a perfume for the body, ruling that its presence does not constitute impurity (*najis*) in this context. This ruling is harmonized with other traditions by interpreting it as referring to the sensory or functional aspect of scent rather than the liquid's inherent ritual impurity, reflecting the Shia scholarly principle of reconciling apparent contradictions through contextual meaning (*ma'na*).
